title: The fourth-moment tail bound is the concentration bound this carrier can state; Hoeffding is blocked on the joint law, not on the exponential
statement: Let X be a rational-valued random variable on a finite index range [0, n) with a distribution p, and let a be a positive rational. Then a^4 times the expectation of the indicator of the event {(X - E X)^4 >= a^4} is at most E[(X - E X)^4] -- i.e. P(|X - E X| >= a) <= E[(X - E X)^4]/a^4, multiplied through so that no Rat.inv appears. It is Rat.markov_constructed at threshold a^4 against the summand ((X - E X)^2)^2, whose nonnegativity is Rat.sq_nonneg applied to (X - E X)^2 rather than to X - E X, and whose threshold positivity is Rat.mul_pos twice. No hypothesis beyond Markov's own. This is the tail bound reached INSTEAD of Hoeffding, and the two obstructions to Hoeffding are structural rather than effort. First, Hoeffding needs E[prod_j f(X_j)] = prod_j E[f(X_j)], a statement about a joint law over a product space, and a shape_search over 4,260 declarations including every constructed carrier finds no product or joint distribution of any spelling. Second, Hoeffding's lemma needs exp on the carrier the moments live on: CReal.expFn DOES exist, but the functional equation e^(x+y) = e^x * e^y -- without which the product step is not even statable -- does not, in the same index.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.fourth_moment_inequality : forall (a : Rat) (X p : Nat -> Rat) (n : Nat), Rat.IsDistribution p n -> Rat.lt Rat.zero a -> Rat.le (Rat.mul (Rat.mul (Rat.mul a a) (Rat.mul a a)) (Rat.expectation (Rat.indicator (Rat.mul (Rat.mul a a) (Rat.mul a a)) (fun k => Rat.mul (Rat.mul (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n)) (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n))) (Rat.mul (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n)) (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n))))) p n)) (Rat.expectation (fun k => Rat.mul (Rat.mul (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n)) (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n))) (Rat.mul (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n)) (Rat.sub (X k) (Rat.expectation X p n)))) p n)

evidence.supports: The declaration is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with an empty Kernel::axiom_footprint, together with every other declaration of ADR-1631's rational binomial layer. The test asserts Environment::contains FIRST, because an absent name has an empty footprint too.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib rat_prelude::binomial_rat::binomial_rat_tests::binomial_rat_declarations_are_axiom_free -- --exact 2>&1 | grep -c '^test result: ok. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: grep -c, not grep -q: -q would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail, and -c exits 1 printing 0 when the line is absent, so a suite that compiled to zero tests and exited 0 is caught rather than counted as a pass. --release is mandatory: the rational prelude SIGABRTs on the default debug thread stack.

notes: What this does NOT give is Hoeffding's RATE. Turning a fourth-moment bound into a better-than-Chebyshev rate needs E[(S - E S)^4] <= 3(m sigma^2)^2, which needs 4-wise uncorrelatedness -- a hypothesis this development CAN state, because it is about covariance-like quantities rather than about a joint law -- and whose proof is a genuine expansion of a fourth power over m terms. That is the next slice and it is bounded.
